links.outcome: F1-score of AI model versus existing in-house triage protocol for incident severity
links.effect: Absolute F1 gains over the existing protocol of 18.46% (life-threatening level), 25.96% (response delay) and 3.63% (jurisdiction); also beat non-continual learning baselines by 3.04%, 9.66% and 0.58%.
links.quote: Compared with the Valencian Region's existing in-house triage protocol, E2eDeepEMC<sup>2</sup> achieved absolute F1-score gains of 18.46% for life-threatening level, 25.96% for response delay and 3.63% for jurisdiction.

unlisted_practices: Continual learning to cope with temporal data distribution drift in predictive models

screen.reason: The study develops and retrospectively evaluates a multimodal triage model and explicitly tests continual learning strategies to handle temporal distribution drift, comparing against non-continual learning baselines.
